grammar.title: 不对 for "wrong/incorrect"
grammar.explanation: 不对 (búduì) is a fixed phrase meaning "wrong" or "incorrect", used as a complete predicate on its own: 这不对 ("This is wrong"). It's a quick way to correct someone or point out a mistake.

grammar.title: 常/常常 for "often"
grammar.explanation: 常 (cháng) means "often", and doubling it to 常常 (chángcháng) makes the same meaning a little more emphatic and conversational. Both go directly before the verb, just like other frequency adverbs such as 也 and 都.

sentences.en: What do you want to do?

sentences.zh: 那个唱歌的人是我朋友。
sentences.pinyin: Nàge chànggē de rén shì wǒ péngyou.
sentences.en: The person singing is my friend.

sentences.zh: 开车的那个人是我爸爸。
sentences.pinyin: Kāichē de nàge rén shì wǒ bàba.
sentences.en: The person driving is my dad.
